entries.review: The boundary follows the hall's south roof end; only the hall supports its complete bitmap among the audited building meshes. The receiving anchor is on adjacent ground. This static projectile-only mask has no character threshold, obstacle links or patch references. Projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

The boundary follows the hall's north roof end; only the hall supports its complete bitmap among the audited building meshes. The receiving anchor is on adjacent ground. This static projectile-only mask has no character threshold, obstacle links or patch references. Projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

The mask follows the east curtain's inner parapet; only this asset fully supports its bitmap among the audited building meshes. Its receiving navigation and flat 150.001-unit surface belong to the same curtain. Character thresholds use that plane, including their extension beyond navigation. This static mask has no obstacle links or patch references. Projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

The mask follows the west curtain's inner parapet; only this asset fully supports its bitmap among the audited building meshes. Its receiving navigation and flat 150.001-unit surface belong to the same curtain. Character thresholds use that plane, including their extension beyond navigation. This static mask has no obstacle links or patch references. Projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

Stair obstacle and receiving surface belong to the postern. Full coverage lifts onto the published postern mesh. The anchor is the stair top-plane centroid; projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

Platform obstacle belongs to the postern. Full coverage lifts onto the published postern mesh. The receiving anchor is on adjacent ground, not the elevated platform; projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.

Both linked tower obstacles belong to the upper gatehouse. This static mask has no patch references. Coverage lifts onto the gatehouse assembly mesh; the receiving anchor is on adjacent ground. Projectile boundaries use the world XY datum.
